text:
The Nifty 500 closed at 23,734.2, down 0.55% on the day, while the Bank Nifty slipped to 61,034.1, a 0.79% decline. Both indices were broadly weaker, with advances (159) far outnumbered by declines (335) and a breadth score of 75.7 indicating a “healthy” but still bearish market environment. The India VIX fell to 15.49, down 6.77%, suggesting lower volatility despite the sell‑off.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding INR 5,736.55 crore, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 2,253.58 crore, extending a 12‑day buying streak for FIIs and a 10‑day selling streak for DIIs. The leading sectors were PSU banks, capital markets and auto, whereas FMCG, manufacturing and energy lagged. Options data show a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.83 for NIFTY and 1.24 for BANK NIFTY, with max‑pain levels around 25,100 and 59,000 respectively; the call wall sits at 26,000 (NIFTY) and 61,000 (BANK NIFTY), while the put wall is near 24,000 and 60,500.

Watch the 2,500‑2,600 point range for NIFTY (pivot P 25,148, S1 25,050, R1 25,242) and the 60,700‑61,300 band for BANK NIFTY (pivot 61,038, S1 60,776, R1 61,296). Key headlines to monitor include RBI rate‑hike concerns, profit‑taking after recent gains, and upcoming IPOs such as Airtel Payments Bank and Razorpay, which could add fresh liquidity or trigger further volatility.
